payload.prompt: Die Gesamtkosten sind von Januar bis Februar 2026 deutlich gestiegen. Analysieren Sie das Hauptbuch und identifizieren Sie die drei Aufwandskonten mit dem größten Anstieg. Erstellen Sie für jedes der drei Konten ein internes Projekt mit dem Kontonamen. Erstellen Sie außerdem eine Aktivität für jedes Projekt.

payload.goal: Analyse the general ledger for January vs February 2026, identify the three expense accounts with the largest increase, then create one internal project per account named after the account and create one activity for each project.
success_checks: General ledger comparison between January and February 2026 is completed.
Exactly three expense accounts with the largest increase are identified and documented.
Three internal projects are created, each named after one identified account.
One activity is created and linked to each created project.
risk_notes: No ledger data or account balances are provided in the prompt; analysis depends on available accounting data.
'Expense account' may require filtering by account class/range according to the company chart of accounts.
Activity creation may require module support or a specific activity endpoint/configuration.
Internal project may require project type/status/manager fields not specified in the prompt.
payload.suggested_first_action: Fetch the general ledger entries or account balances for 2026-01 and 2026-02 and compute the increase per expense account.
ordered_steps: GET general ledger balances or transactions for period 2026-01 filtered to expense accounts.
GET general ledger balances or transactions for period 2026-02 filtered to expense accounts.
Aggregate by account and calculate February minus January change for each expense account.
Sort descending by increase and select the top 3 accounts.
For each selected account, POST /project with internal project settings and name equal to the account name.
For each created project, POST activity linked to the project with a default internal activity name if required by API.
Verify each project and activity was created successfully and linked correctly.

planned_endpoints.summary: Create customer. Related customer addresses may also be created.
Find employees corresponding with sent data.

rules: When email is provided, ALWAYS set BOTH email AND invoiceEmail to the same value.
Do NOT send isCustomer (it's readOnly and auto-set).
For addresses, use postalAddress={addressLine1, postalCode, city, country={id: 161}} for Norway.
ALWAYS search first: GET /employee?email=<email> — the sandbox often has pre-existing employees. Reuse if found.
Only POST /employee if GET returns 0 results.
When POSTing, ALWAYS include department={"id": dept_id}. Create department first if needed.
userType should be 'STANDARD' unless admin is explicitly requested.
Requires customer={"id": customer_id} and projectManager={"id": employee_id}.
startDate is REQUIRED — use today_iso from execution_brief if prompt doesn't specify a date.
If the prompt mentions a project number (prosjektnummer), set number=<project_number>.
isInternal should be false unless explicitly stated as internal project.
If description text is provided, set description=<text>.
For fixed-price projects, set isFixedPrice=true and fixedPrice=<amount> (camelCase).
Requires project={"id": project_id} and activity={"id": activity_id}.
If activity already linked (409), ignore the error and proceed.
If a default hourly rate already exists (409 Duplicate entry), GET /project/hourlyRates?projectId=... then PUT to update it.

payload.headline: Wrong top-3 expense accounts identified; only 1/6 checks passed despite clean execution
what_went_wrong: The agent's ledger analysis produced incorrect top-3 accounts — only Check 5 passed, suggesting the account ranking (7100, 6500, 5000) was wrong vs. expected results.
The agent fetched /ledger/posting twice for each month (4 calls total) but the data was 'trimmed', meaning pagination or field selection was insufficient to capture all postings.
The agent may have missed postings due to not paginating through all results, leading to incomplete aggregation and wrong account totals.
The agent used /ledger/posting without specifying account type filters or ensuring all pages were retrieved, risking incomplete data for the comparison.
what_worked: Project creation and activity linking executed cleanly with 0 errors — all 6 POST calls succeeded.
The agent correctly identified the need for internal projects and used isInternal=true with a valid project manager.
what_to_try_next: Use /ledger (not /ledger/posting) with dateFrom/dateTo and account range filters, and paginate with count/from params to ensure ALL postings are captured before aggregating.
Cross-check account totals by using /account or /ledger with grouping to verify aggregated balances rather than summing individual postings that may be truncated.

After identifying top-3 accounts, verify the ranking against the raw data before creating projects — add a validation step comparing account numbers to expected expense ranges (4000-7999 in Norwegian chart of accounts).
unnecessary_calls: GET /activity — fetching existing activities was unnecessary since the agent could create a new activity per project instead.
Duplicate GET /ledger/posting calls (4 total for 2 months) — the first pair returned trimmed data and were effectively wasted calls without pagination.
